title: The Best Cold Brew Maker for Hot Southern Summers
dek: When it's 95° with 90% humidity, nobody wants hot coffee. Make a week of cold brew for less than two café drinks.
intro: Down here, iced coffee season runs from about March to November. Cold brew is the easiest way to keep up: coarse grounds, cold water, 12 to 18 hours in the fridge, strain. Done.
Any jar can make cold brew. What a dedicated maker buys you is easy straining, less mess, and a pitcher that fits in your fridge.
how_we_picked: We picked makers that are easy to strain and clean and that fit in a real fridge. Specs are from the Amazon listings.

picks.verdict: Fits the fridge door, airtight lid, shatter resistant. The one we'd buy first.
Even water distribution and a fine filter make a clean, low-grit concentrate.
Half a gallon in a glass mason jar. Great for porches, crowds, and tailgates.
Slim glass pitcher. Grounds in, water in, wait.

bar_tip: Use a coarse grind (like rough sea salt) and about 1 cup of coffee to 4 cups of water for concentrate. Cut it 1:1 with water or milk over ice.

faq.q: How long does cold brew last?
faq.a: Most people keep it 1 to 2 weeks in the fridge; it tastes best in the first week.
Iced coffee is hot coffee chilled. Cold brew never sees heat, so it's smoother and less acidic.
Medium to dark roasts. Chocolatey, nutty coffees shine as cold brew.
